why: Checked where the guarantee is kept rather than where it is made: test/README.md gives it the whole `deps:` conformance group with a row saying exactly what is asserted, and oca/README.md's opening line calls the bridge zero-dependency. The claim that it appears only in SPEC 8.5 is false.
The recommendation listed nouns rather than naming a document somebody could sit down and write.

set.recommendation: Write README.md with these sections, each answering one question: what ponder is and the problem it solves; install (install.sh and the symlink into both harnesses); the loop as one diagram; a 60-second quickstart that runs; the full command table; the convergence signals table; OCA integration and how to turn it off; where the lenses live and how to add one.

why: Every earlier finding graded a document against the code it describes. Nobody had graded the code against the documents, which is the only direction that catches a documented feature nobody built.

finding.title: `--mode build` is documented but unimplemented
finding.detail: `ponder start --mode deliberate|build` is in SPEC 5's usage line, SPEC 3.1 defines build as 'deltas may touch disk', and protocol.md:91 gives it a table row reading 'build permits deltas that touch disk'. In lib/, `session.mode` is validated at cli.js:517, stored, and read exactly once more — report.md:57 prints it. No delta path branches on it. A reader who starts a session with --mode build gets deliberate-mode behaviour and no warning.
finding.recommendation: Either mark build as reserved-and-unimplemented everywhere it appears, or have `ponder start --mode build` refuse with a message saying so. Documenting a flag that silently does nothing is worse than not offering it.

why: Both readings of the --severity wording produce identical behaviour today, so no reader is currently harmed by the ambiguity; it should not outrank findings that cost someone an afternoon.
